purpose: Bound whether the antirez-style exact N=2 MTP verifier can plausibly be a 10 tok/s route for the current vendor DeepSeek4 strict-cold SOTA before implementing loader/runtime code.

n2_bound_math.formula: tok_s = 4.4 * (A + 1) / C_total, where A is average accepted draft tokens and C_total is target-verification plus MTP-draft cost in current one-token target-pass units.

required_for_10_tok_s.decision: cannot reach 10 even with one current-token cost
minimum acceptance threshold, leaves zero room for verifier/draft overhead
requires target verification plus draft to add less than 22.7ms over current one-token pass
best possible N=2 case; only 72.7ms extra over current one-token pass is allowed

why_current_vendor_cannot_assume_this_bo: The current accepted decode path is dominated by CPU up/down fallback, averaging about 139.9ms per token just for that component.

An exact N=2 verifier must compute target logits for the drafted suffix. Unless target MoE verification is substantially sublinear, the second verified token alone can consume more than the entire 72.7ms extra budget.

Existing current-head work has already rejected CPU batch rewrite, raw/transposed/row-tile exact hot-batch kernels, MMVQ skip/write, source-only overlap, and full up/down CUDA/streaming as 10 tok/s routes.
The MTP draft itself has nonzero cost: it needs an extra supplementary attention/MoE layer, MTP raw cache, output head work, and extra file/VRAM/page-cache accounting.
The 3.807GB MTP GGUF adds TTFT and 16GB page-cache pressure. Full preload was already rejected by TTFT math.
The antirez reference README states the current MTP/speculative path is experimental, correctness-gated, and provides at most slight speedup, not a meaningful generation-speed win.

notes: This does not prove MTP cannot produce a small token-rate gain. It only rejects MTP as an efficient path toward 10 tok/s under the current constraints.
Do not implement MTP loader/verifier unless the objective changes to small SOTA gains or a new MTP/DSpark implementation supports A>=5 with measured sublinear target verification.

next_direction_after_rejection: Do not spend runtime-source work on antirez exact N=2 MTP for the 10 tok/s objective.
Return to non-MTP mechanisms only if they first provide a hard-bound above 10 tok/s.
The only remaining plausible class is a genuinely new exact compact representation or target-verification mechanism that removes most CPU up/down fallback without serial target work.
